feedback.problem: What is the coefficient of $(x-1)^{3}$ in the third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x}$ about $x=1?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficient of $(x-1)^{3}$ is $\frac{1}{3!}{f}^{(3)}(1).$ Let's compute the necessary derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt[3]{x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-2/3} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\frac{2}{9}{x}^{-5/3} \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =\frac{10}{27}{x}^{-8/3}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${f}^{‴}(1),$ which gives

$$
{f}^{‴}(-1)=\frac{10}{27}\cdot {1}^{-8/3}=\frac{10}{27}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{3!}{f}^{‴}(1)=\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{10}{27}=\frac{5}{81}.
$$

So the coefficient of $(x-1)^{3}$ is $\frac{5}{81}.$
